domain_label: System->Subject->Topic Catalog Schema & Collapsible-Tree Information Architecture
purpose: A method for turning the KB1 blueprint spine into a browsable study catalog: a system->subject->topic->item hierarchy layered over the knowledge graph, mapped from each exam's native axes onto ONE collapsible tree with the remaining axes as orthogonal pathology/physiology/everything facet tags, portal/alias nodes so a topic appears under multiple parents without duplication, a per-item ordering surface (logic deferred to sched), and the collapse->expand, click-heading-to-start UX contract — grounded in structural patterns only (Anki decks/tags, RemNote portals/priorities, UWorld matrix selector, Osmosis reorderable/shareable playlists) with progress rollup deferred to engage, content to contenteng, and KG truth to kgraph/kgverify.
assumptions: the KB1 blueprint spine is the input this schema maps onto one browsable tree; this KB does not re-author blueprints
the tool-pattern grounding (Anki, RemNote, UWorld, Osmosis) borrows STRUCTURAL patterns only with a [FACT-source] citation each and copies no proprietary content, weights, question banks or videos
curric owns the hierarchy/tree information architecture and the per-item ordering SURFACE; it owns neither the sequencing logic (sched) nor the progress rollup (engage)
catalog leaves attach onto knowledge-graph concepts owned by kgraph, whose truth is judged by kgverify; curric attaches, it does not own the KG
the studiable content in each leaf is produced by contenteng; curric arranges it, it does not author it
exclusions: the prerequisite/adaptive sequencing logic, interval and BKT math (sched+learner)
the progress/mastery rollup and gamification rendered on the tree (engage+uxguide)
the knowledge-graph proposition schema (kgraph) and proposition truth (kgverify)
the studiable content decomposition and card authoring inside each item (contenteng)
the catalog-object sharing / multi-user model (KB3) and the exam blueprints themselves (KB1)

glossary.definition: The catalog schema curric owns: a four-level tree layered over the knowledge graph (SYSTEM browse axis -> SUBJECT grouping -> TOPIC studiable unit -> ITEM leaf slot) into which the KB1 blueprint spine is mapped as one browsable tree. [FACT — KB scope]

The organizing principle: the tree (decks) controls structure/containment while tags control orthogonal cross-cutting function; it grounds the tree/facet split and keeps facets as tags rather than branches. [FACT-source: docs.ankiweb.net — Anki decks vs hierarchical tags pattern]

A cross-cutting filter (pathology / physiology / 'everything', discipline-wise, per-subject) modeled as a tag ORTHOGONAL to the tree and evaluated as a query over tagged leaves — never a second parallel hierarchy. [FACT — IA method]

A node that surfaces a single source topic under multiple parents by reference, so one topic can live under several axes without duplication. [FACT-source: help.remnote.com portals article — the portal pattern]

The Review-selector UX: collapsed-by-default, expand-on-click, shallow default depth, lazy-rendered large branches, and every heading node itself a launchable study action ('start this branch in order'). [FACT-source: Anki shallow-nesting guidance as a pattern]

The explicit '1st / 2nd / ...' ordering UI and the ordered catalog object, owned by curric; the ordering LOGIC (prereq/adaptive/interval) is deferred to sched+learner. Grounded in the RemNote folder-priorities pattern. [FACT-source: remnote.com folder-priorities feature — priority-ordering pattern]

The hard rule that exactly one primary containment tree exists; alternate axes, disciplines and browse modes are realized as facet tags or portals, never as a second parallel hierarchy that could diverge. [FACT — invariant]

A reserved position on each tree node where a completion bar / mastery badge / gamification token renders; curric defines the slot geometry while engage+uxguide compute and fill the rollup — which is why the tree currently reads all-zeros. [FACT — remit boundary]

The tree leaf that attaches onto a knowledge-graph concept (owned by kgraph, truth by kgverify) and holds contenteng-produced content; curric owns its position and provenance trace, not its content or the concept's truth. [FACT — interface contract]

The discipline of borrowing STRUCTURAL patterns (tree, tags-as-facets, portals, reorderable playlists, subject x system matrix selector) from Anki, RemNote, UWorld and Osmosis with a [FACT-source] citation each, while copying NO proprietary content, weights, question banks or videos. [FACT — grounding policy]

Each type has a defined parent/child contract; the leaf ITEM is the interface to KB1's studiable slot. [FACT — schema]

nodes.definition: PORTAL / ALIAS nodes let one topic appear under multiple parents WITHOUT duplicating it: the topic exists once and is surfaced by reference elsewhere. This is the RemNote 'portals' pattern (structural pattern only, no proprietary content). It resolves the reality that a studiable topic often belongs under several axes (e.g. a pharmacology topic under both a Discipline facet and an Organ-System subject) while keeping a single source node. [FACT-source: https://help.remnote.com/en/articles/6030742-portals — the portal pattern]

included: portal/alias nodes surfacing one topic under many parents by reference

excluded: copying a topic into multiple places (duplication)

[FACT-source: https://docs.ankiweb.net/ — decks/subdecks vs hierarchical tags]

nodes.definition: The collapsible-tree contract, part 1: the tree renders COLLAPSED BY DEFAULT and EXPANDS ON CLICK, with a SHALLOW default nesting depth (the Anki shallow-nesting guidance, 1-2 visible levels before drill-in) and LAZY RENDERING of large branches. This keeps the 'Review' selector scannable rather than an overwhelming wall. [FACT-source: https://ankiweb.net/shared/info/1172858842; https://docs.ankiweb.net/ — shallow-nesting guidance as a pattern]

nodes.definition: The collapsible-tree contract, part 2: EVERY HEADING NODE IS ITSELF A LAUNCHABLE STUDY ACTION — clicking a heading can start that entire branch in order, not merely toggle disclosure. The order in which a branch's items launch is the per-item ordering surface (see PER_ITEM_ORDERING), whose logic is deferred to sched. [FACT — UX contract]

nodes.definition: A hard invariant: there is exactly ONE primary containment tree; a facet, a discipline lens, or an alternate axis is NEVER implemented as a second parallel hierarchy. All cross-cutting slicing lives in the orthogonal tag/facet layer or via portal/alias references into the one tree. This prevents the classic drift where 'browse by discipline' silently becomes a rival tree that diverges from 'browse by system'. [FACT — invariant]

included: exactly one primary containment tree
all alternate axes as facets/portals, never parallel trees
excluded: a second hierarchy for a secondary axis
divergent rival trees for different browse modes

nodes.definition: The synthesis: the catalog IA is the UNION of a shallow collapsible TREE for structure + orthogonal TAG-FACETS for functional slicing (pathology/physiology/everything) + PORTAL/ALIAS nodes to avoid duplication + REORDERABLE, SHAREABLE catalog OBJECTS with a per-item ordering surface — every heading launchable, ordering logic deferred to sched, progress slots deferred to engage. This IA is the handoff artifact to KB3's catalog-object/sharing model. [FACT — synthesis]

included: tree + facet tags + portals + reorderable shareable objects as the IA union
the handoff to KB3's catalog model
excluded: the sequencing and progress math (sched, engage)

conflict_axes.name: facet_as_tag_vs_second_tree
conflict_axes.description: An alternate browse axis tempts a second parallel hierarchy while the honest design keeps it an orthogonal facet tag.
poles: build a second parallel tree for the axis
keep the axis a facet tag over one tree
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: one primary tree; every alternate axis is a facet or portal, never a second tree

conflict_axes.name: ordering_surface_vs_sequencing_logic
conflict_axes.description: Owning the 1st/2nd ordering UI tempts curric to compute the sequence that sched owns.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: own the ordering surface only; request the sequence from sched and render it

conflict_axes.name: duplicate_topic_vs_portal
conflict_axes.description: A topic belonging under several parents tempts duplication while portals keep one source.
poles: copy the topic into each parent
portal one source node into many parents
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use portal/alias nodes; never duplicate a topic

conflict_axes.name: deep_tree_vs_shallow_default
conflict_axes.description: Rich structure tempts deep nesting while scannability wants a shallow collapsed default.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default shallow and collapsed; expand on click; lazy-render depth

conflict_axes.name: pattern_vs_proprietary_copy
conflict_axes.description: Grounding in real tools tempts copying proprietary content while only structural patterns may be borrowed.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: borrow patterns with a [FACT-source] citation; copy no proprietary content

conflict_axes.name: define_slot_vs_fill_it
conflict_axes.description: A visible progress slot or content slot tempts curric to fill it while filling belongs to engage/contenteng.
poles: curric defines the slot, sibling fills it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: curric owns slot geometry; engage fills progress, contenteng fills content

conflict_axes.name: heading_toggle_vs_launch
conflict_axes.description: A heading with two affordances tempts collapsing them, losing either disclosure or launch.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: give headings both affordances, visually disambiguated

conflict_axes.name: own_kg_vs_attach_to_kg
conflict_axes.description: Attaching items to KG concepts tempts curric to reshape or judge the KG it does not own.
poles: curric attaches onto the KG, deferring schema/truth
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: attach only; defer KG schema to kgraph and truth to kgverify

edge_cases.description: A 'browse by discipline' mode is built as its own hierarchy alongside 'browse by system'
edge_cases.trigger: a secondary axis wanting its own tree
edge_cases.mitigation: implement discipline browsing as a facet tag over the one tree, never a second parallel tree

edge_cases.description: A user asks curric to compute the correct prerequisite order of a branch
edge_cases.trigger: a sequencing request at the ordering surface
edge_cases.mitigation: render the ordering surface and route the prereq/adaptive computation to sched+learner

edge_cases.description: A pharmacology topic needed under both Pharmacology and Cardiovascular is copied into both
edge_cases.mitigation: portal one source node into both parents; do not duplicate the topic

edge_cases.description: The Review selector renders fully expanded with hundreds of nodes
edge_cases.mitigation: render collapsed-by-default with shallow depth and lazy-render large branches

edge_cases.description: A pathology facet misses leaves that were never tagged pathology
edge_cases.mitigation: treat facet completeness as a tagging data-quality requirement; surface untagged leaves for tagging

edge_cases.description: A build copies a UWorld-style question bank to fill the matrix selector
edge_cases.trigger: proprietary content copied under a pattern
edge_cases.mitigation: borrow the selector pattern only; fill it with contenteng content, never copied proprietary items

edge_cases.description: Every tree node shows a 0% progress bar and it looks broken
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the tree defines slots and engage fills them; the zeros mean engage rollup is pending, not a bug

edge_cases.description: A heading click launches the whole branch when the user meant to expand it
edge_cases.mitigation: visually separate the disclosure toggle from the 'start branch' action on each heading

edge_cases.description: A catalog leaf surfaces a mis-modeled KG concept and curric is asked to fix it
edge_cases.trigger: a KG error at a catalog leaf
edge_cases.mitigation: route the KG-schema fix to kgraph and the truth question to kgverify; curric only re-attaches

edge_cases.description: A user asks curric to decompose a textbook chapter into the topic's cards
edge_cases.trigger: a content-decomposition request at the catalog
edge_cases.mitigation: route decomposition to contenteng; curric positions the item slot it will fill

edge_cases.description: TOEFL's four sections leave almost no SUBJECT layer between SYSTEM and ITEM
edge_cases.trigger: an exam axis that fits the node types thinly
edge_cases.mitigation: allow a thin or optional SUBJECT layer; keep the four node types without forcing an artificial subject

workflow.action: Define the system/subject/topic/item schema over the KG
workflow.description: Establish the hierarchy as a schema into which the KB1 spine maps
workflow.gate: the schema is defined as a shelf over the KG with content/sequencing/progress deferred

workflow.description: Define system/subject/topic/item with parent/child contracts and the ITEM leaf interface
workflow.gate: the four node types and the ITEM-as-interface leaf are specified

workflow.action: Map exam axes onto one tree
workflow.description: Project each exam's axes onto one tree with a single primary spine axis
workflow.gate: each exam maps to one tree with one primary axis and the rest as facets

workflow.description: Represent pathology/physiology/everything and discipline/per-subject as tags, not branches
workflow.gate: facets are orthogonal tags queried over the tree, never a second tree

workflow.description: Let one topic appear under many parents via portals without duplication
workflow.gate: multi-parent topics use portals with a single source, no duplication
the tree collapses by default, expands on click, and headings are launchable

workflow.description: Provide the 1st/2nd ordering UI and ordered catalog object
workflow.gate: curric owns the ordering surface and defers the sequencing logic to sched

workflow.action: Ground the IA in tool patterns only
workflow.description: Cite Anki/RemNote/UWorld/Osmosis patterns with [FACT-source], copy no proprietary content
workflow.gate: every borrowed concept is a cited structural pattern with no proprietary content

workflow.action: Define progress slots and KG/content boundaries
workflow.description: Reserve progress slots (engage fills), attach items to KG concepts (kgraph/kgverify), defer content (contenteng)
workflow.gate: progress rollup, KG truth and content are deferred to engage, kgverify and contenteng

workflow.description: Combine tree + facets + portals + reorderable shareable objects as the IA handoff to KB3
workflow.gate: the IA is the union preserving the one-tree invariant and handing sharing to KB3

priority_rationale: The hierarchy frame and node types come first because every mapping, facet and UX rule inherits the system/subject/topic/item schema; the axis-to-tree mapping, facet-as-tag model and one-tree invariant come next because they set how blueprints browse without fragmenting into rival trees; the collapse/expand + click-to-start contract and the per-item ordering surface (deferred to sched) define the interaction; the tool-pattern grounding and patterns-only discipline keep it defensible; the boundary nodes (progress slots, KG attachment, content deferral) fix what curric does not fill; and the IA synthesis closes the KB as the handoff to KB3.

dominance_rules.rule: The one-tree invariant dominates any second parallel hierarchy
dominance_rules.rationale: rival trees diverge and fragment the catalog
dominance_rules.trigger: an alternate axis or browse mode wants its own tree
dominance_rules.action: realize it as a facet tag or portal over the one tree

dominance_rules.rule: Sched ownership of sequencing dominates the ordering surface
dominance_rules.rationale: curric owns the UI but not the prereq/adaptive math
dominance_rules.trigger: a request needs the true order computed
dominance_rules.action: render the ordering surface and defer the sequence to sched+learner

dominance_rules.rationale: a duplicated topic diverges across copies
dominance_rules.trigger: a topic belongs under several parents
dominance_rules.action: portal one source node into many parents; never duplicate

dominance_rules.rationale: copied content/weights are undefensible and out of scope
dominance_rules.trigger: grounding a feature in a real tool
dominance_rules.action: borrow the structural pattern with a [FACT-source] citation; copy no proprietary content

dominance_rules.rationale: progress, KG truth and content are owned by siblings
dominance_rules.trigger: a progress/content/KG slot needs a value
dominance_rules.action: curric defines the slot; engage fills progress, contenteng fills content, kgverify judges truth

dominance_rules.rule: Shallow collapse-by-default dominates a fully-expanded tree
dominance_rules.action: collapse by default, shallow depth, expand on click, lazy render

dominance_rules.rationale: a learner should start a whole branch from its heading
dominance_rules.action: give the heading both disclosure and 'start branch' affordances, disambiguated

dominance_rules.rationale: KG schema and truth belong to kgraph and kgverify
dominance_rules.trigger: an item attaches onto a KG concept
dominance_rules.action: attach only; defer schema to kgraph and truth to kgverify

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assert the one-tree invariant before adding any browse mode
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second parallel hierarchy that later diverges and must be merged back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark facets as tags, not branches, at creation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a facet growing into a rival tree that has to be un-built

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label the ordering surface as sched-fed the first time it is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: curric later computing a sequence that must be retracted to sched

anti_rework_rules.rule: Use portals for multi-parent topics from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: duplicated topics that later diverge across copies

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cite a [FACT-source] pattern for each borrowed tool concept at creation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a feature later found to have copied proprietary content

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reserve progress slots as engage-filled from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: curric wiring a progress computation that must be handed to engage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Default the tree to collapsed and shallow before populating it
Define the ITEM leaf as a KG/content interface at creation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the leaf later absorbing content or KG-truth ownership it must defer

iteration_protocol.trigger: sched publishes its prereq/adaptive ordering interface
iteration_protocol.action: wire the per-item ordering surface to consume sched's sequence and stop rendering any placeholder order

iteration_protocol.trigger: engage publishes its progress/mastery rollup interface
iteration_protocol.action: bind the reserved progress slots to engage's rollup, replacing the all-zeros placeholders
bind ITEM leaves to contenteng content, filling the studiable slots

iteration_protocol.trigger: kgraph revises the concept schema or attachment interface
iteration_protocol.action: re-attach catalog items onto the revised KG concepts without judging their truth

iteration_protocol.trigger: user testing shows the default tree depth or heading affordances confuse users
iteration_protocol.action: tune the collapse depth and disambiguate the disclose/launch affordances

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new facet dimension or exam axis is added
iteration_protocol.action: add it as an orthogonal tag or portal, preserving the one-tree invariant
